title: Vertical and horizontal pasting of underived clopen comparison maps
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. All schemes are finite-type $k$-schemes; their structure maps are not required to be separated [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For each $T$, choose either $\mathscr M_T=\operatorname{Mod}((A_n)_T)$ at one fixed $n$, or the category $\mathscr M_T$ of module sheaves $M_n$ over $(A_n)_T$ with semilinear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{A_{n+1}\to A_n}M_n$ and compatible componentwise morphisms [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived category $D(\mathscr M_T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a scheme map $f$ write $f^*$ for exact constant-coefficient module inverse image and $P_f=D(f^*)$; for an open immersion $j$ write $j_!$ for exact extension by zero and $J_j=D(j_!)$. Use the specified adjunctions $P_f\dashv S_f=Rf_*$ and $J_j\dashv P_j$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. System operations are constructed simultaneously on the ringed diagram site, before finite evaluation, scalar restriction or total limit [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

For each commutative square $Q$ with top $k_1:U\hookrightarrow V$, bottom $i:W\hookrightarrow Z$ quasi-compact open, and verticals $r:U\to W$, $p:V\to Z$ proper, let $b:V\times_ZW\to V$, $q:V\times_ZW\to W$, $s=(k_1,r):U\to V\times_ZW$ be the fibre-product maps [def-pc-fibre-product]. Use the clopen projector $\pi_s$ (identity on $s(U)$, zero on its complementary open) and the open-unit-normalized $\widetilde\beta:p^*i_!\cong b_!q^*$ to define the underived map
$$\widetilde a_Q:p^*i_!\xrightarrow{\widetilde\beta}b_!q^*\xrightarrow{b_!\pi_sq^*}b_!s_!s^*q^*\cong(k_1)_!r^*.$$
The compositors here are the canonical adjunction-normalized module-sheaf compositors [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization].

For three rows $U_a\xrightarrow{j_a}V_a$ ($a=0,1,2$) of quasi-compact opens and proper verticals $r_a:U_{a-1}\to U_a$, $p_a:V_{a-1}\to V_a$, with $p_aj_{a-1}=j_ar_a$ ($a=1,2$), put
$$A=(\widetilde a_{Q_1}r_2^*)\circ(p_1^*\widetilde a_{Q_2}):p_1^*p_2^*(j_2)_!\to(j_0)_!r_1^*r_2^*.$$
Under the canonical compositors, restriction of both factors along $j_0$ is identity on $r_1^*r_2^*$, and $A=\widetilde a_{Q_{\rm out}}$ for the outer square.

For horizontally adjacent squares with top opens $k_1:U\to V$, $k_2:V\to T$, bottom opens $i_1:W\to Z$, $i_2:Z\to Y$, proper verticals $r,p,q$, and $pk_1=i_1r$, $qk_2=i_2p$, put
$$B=((k_2)_!\widetilde a_{Q_1})\circ(\widetilde a_{Q_2}(i_1)_!):q^*(i_2)_!(i_1)_!\to(k_2)_!(k_1)_!r^*.$$
Restriction of both factors along $k_2k_1$ is identity on $r^*$, and $B=\widetilde a_{Q_{\rm out}}$ under the same compositors. Both equalities are equalities of natural transformations on module sheaves or on semilinear module systems, before deriving. Squares with identity verticals or identity horizontals give identity $\widetilde a$ under the canonical units. No Cartesian hypothesis on any square, boundedness, constructibility or normalized-system condition is imposed.

proof.text: For ordinary vertical pasting, conjugate the pasted transformation by the inverse-image compositors. The proved source-library upperStarCompIso_hom_app_paste identifies the outer square comparison with the two inner comparisons. Naturality of that comparison and of the open unit, followed by the two normalization equations, proves normalization of the conjugated paste. Proper maps compose by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. Apply the uniqueness clause from Step 1 and cancel the compositor isomorphisms. Naturality gives the first factor restriction; the second is the first square normalization.

source.place: Tags 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose) and 0F7D (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal). Agent underived clopen-restriction formulation on pro-etale modules and semilinear systems; returned proof Steps 7 and 8 and identity part of Step 10.

proof.text: For ordinary horizontal pasting, expand the unit of the composite open adjunction using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Naturality of the first square comparison moves the second open unit through it, and the second square normalization cancels the second factor. Naturality of the second open unit and the first normalization complete the composite normalization equation. The conjugate-iso unit equation for Adjunction.leftAdjointCompIso transports this equation to the specified open compositors. The proved source-library pullback-square pasting law identifies the outer square comparison. Uniqueness from Step 1 and cancellation give horizontal pasting. The same two normalization calculations give the two factor equations.

source.place: Tags 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose) and 0F7D (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal). Agent underived clopen-restriction formulation on pro-etale modules and semilinear systems; returned proof Steps 7 and 8 and identity part of Step 10.

proof.text: For systems use the already proved ordinary-system moduleAlpha_vertical and moduleAlpha_horizontal equations of [lem-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-pasting], canceling respectively the pullback and open compositor. The two factor restrictions follow from naturality and the single-square normalization, exactly as at ordinary levels. Package the fixed categorical data of the horizontal factor calculation; the system horizontal assertion records its same two factor equations through this constructed package, avoiding repeated conversion inside chosen functors. The only varying arguments are essentially-small proofs, so proof irrelevance and congruence identify the data packages and transfer the factor predicates between the two existing cached presentations.

source.place: Tags 0F7C (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose) and 0F7D (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open-compose-horizontal). Agent underived clopen-restriction formulation on pro-etale modules and semilinear systems; returned proof Steps 7 and 8 and identity part of Step 10.

proof.text: For identity verticals, the source-library upperStarComp identity laws express the square comparison by the two inverse-image identity isomorphisms. For systems use the ordinary identity compositor laws proved in [lem-sf-semilinear-compositor-coherence]. Naturality of the open unit and cancellation normalize the displayed identity word. For identity horizontals, Adjunction.leftAdjointIdIso is normalized by its conjugate right identity isomorphism: its defining unit equation normalizes the displayed word. The inverse square comparison gives the horizontal identity case. Apply the uniqueness clause from Step 1 in each case. These are categorical equations and cover the empty open and zero module without additional assumptions.
